citations.quote: One pivotal study, VER002-9, has been submitted to provide support for the use of anidulafungin in the treatment of candidemia.

VER002-9 was a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind comparative study to evaluate the safety and efficacy of anidulafungin versus fluconazole in the treatment of candidemia and other forms of invasive candidiasis.

design.text: Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, non-inferiority, multicenter study of anidulafungin versus fluconazole; patients randomized 1:1 to anidulafungin IV (200 mg loading, then 100 mg daily) or fluconazole IV (800 mg loading, 400 mg maintenance).

citations.quote: This is a phase 3, randomized double-blind, non-inferiority multi-center study of the safety and efficacy of anidulafungin vs. fluconazole in the treatment of patients with candidemia and other forms of invasive candidiasis and prevention of complications.

Patients with candidemia and other forms of invasive candidiasis who met the inclusion and exclusion criteria were randomized (1:1 ratio) to treatment with either anidulafungin IV (200mg loading dose followed by 100mg daily maintenance dose) or fluconazole IV (800mg loading dose and 400mg maintenance dose).

population.text: Patients with candidemia and other forms of invasive candidiasis (primarily non-neutropenic).

citations.quote: The efficacy of anidulafungin for the treatment of candidemia in primarily non-neutropenic patients was supported by one controlled study.

endpoint.text: Primary efficacy endpoint was the global response (combined clinical and microbiological) in the microbiological intent-to-treat (Micro-ITT/MITT) population at the end of IV therapy.

citations.quote: The primary efficacy endpoint was the global response (combined clinical and microbiological) in the microbiological intent-to-treat (Micro-ITT) population at the end of IV therapy.

n.text: 261 patients randomized; MITT population 245 (127 anidulafungin, 118 fluconazole).

citations.quote: A total of 261 patients were randomized to receive treatment in VER002-9. The modified intent to treat (MITT) population included 245 patients (127 in the anidulafungin group and 118 in the fluconazole group).

result.text: Global response at end of IV therapy (MITT): 75.6% anidulafungin vs 60.2% fluconazole; between-group difference 15.4% (95% CI 3.0, 27.8), meeting non-inferiority (margin -20%) and establishing statistical superiority since the lower bound exceeded 0.

citations.quote: the success rate was 75.6% for anidulafungin and 60.2% for fluconazole

the 95% confidence interval about the difference in response rates is greater than the non-inferiority margin of -20%. Since the lower limit of the confidence interval is greater than 0, it can be said that anidulafungin was statistically superior to fluconazole in the MITT population.

target_moa.text: Anidulafungin is a semi-synthetic echinocandin (lipopeptide) that non-competitively inhibits 1,3-beta-D-glucan synthase, blocking formation of 1,3-beta-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall not present in mammalian cells.

citations.quote: Anidulafungin is a semi-synthetic echinocandin with antifungal activity. Anidulafungin inhibits glucan synthase, an enzyme present in fungal, but not mammalian cells. This results in inhibition of the formation of 1,3-\beta-D-glucan, an essential component of the fungal cell wall.
Similar to other echinocandins, anidulafungin is a non-competitive inhibitor of (1,3)-\beta-D-glucan synthase.

ERAXIS (anidulafungin) is a semi-synthetic lipopeptide synthesized from a fermentation product of *Aspergillus nidulans*. Anidulafungin is an echinocandin, a class of antifungal drugs that inhibits the synthesis of 1,3-\beta-D-glucan, an essential component of fungal cell walls.

key_safety.text: Generally well tolerated; most frequent treatment-related AEs in the candidemia study (anidulafungin vs fluconazole) were diarrhea (3.1% vs 1.6%) and hypokalemia (3.1% vs 2.4%). Possible infusion-related reactions occurred (28 (13.2%) and 9 (7%) patients in the integrated analysis of safety). Hepatic effects are the main safety concern; a few cases of significant hepatic dysfunction and hepatitis were reported in patients receiving anidulafungin in studies completed since the original NDA submission, though a causal relationship to anidulafungin was not established.

citations.quote: Diarrhea	4 (3.1)	2 (1.6)
Hypokalemia	4 (3.1)	3 (2.4)
In the integrated analysis of safety for this NDA, 28(13.2%) and 9(7%) patients experienced infusion-related reactions.
Overall, anidulafungin was well tolerated. The adverse event of concern was hepatic safety.

In summary, a few cases of significant hepatic dysfunction and hepatitis, were reported in patients receiving anidulafungin in studies completed since the original NDA submission. However, a causal relationship to anidulafungin was not established.

changes.note: Added a verbatim citation (MedR line 365) that directly supports the clause 'a few cases of significant hepatic dysfunction and hepatitis were reported in patients receiving anidulafungin'; also aligned the text to the review's wording including that a causal relationship was not established.

Removed the unsupported anidulafungin-vs-fluconazole group attribution for the infusion-reaction rates since MedR line 77 states '28(13.2%) and 9(7%) patients experienced infusion-related reactions' without labeling which group is which; text now matches the un-labeled review figure and citation is now the complete (non-truncated) verbatim sentence from line 77.

No change: the 2006 label (doc 0b4ee0de, lines 120 and 122) explicitly lists both 'Candidemia and other forms of Candida infections (intra-abdominal abscess, and peritonitis)' and 'Esophageal candidiasis' under INDICATIONS AND USAGE, so esophageal candidiasis is a supported part of this approval; the apparent inconsistency reflects a second study/indication and the field is correctly grounded.

Changed loose label 'Peptide (semi-synthetic lipopeptide echinocandin)' to 'Semi-synthetic lipopeptide echinocandin' to match the cited label language (doc 0b4ee0de line 5) which describes it as a semi-synthetic lipopeptide echinocandin rather than a generic peptide.
